forces.title: LNG dependence threatens industrial hydrogen supply for fertilizers
forces.description: India's ammonia production, essential for nitrogenous fertilizers, relies on hydrogen chemically derived from natural gas. A significant portion of this natural gas is imported as LNG, with high dependency on Gulf-origin supply and chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz. Geopolitical tensions, like those in West Asia, can disrupt LNG flows, leading to price escalation and supply delays for natural gas, which directly impacts industrial hydrogen availability and costs for fertilizer manufacturing. This structural dependence creates systemic fragility for a critical industrial gas input.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

forces.title: Biogas offers domestic pathway for renewable industrial hydrogen
forces.description: Biogas and compressed biogas (CBG) present a potential domestic alternative feedstock for hydrogen production, which is crucial for ammonia and fertilizer manufacturing. By leveraging locally available biomass through anaerobic digestion, upgraded biogas can substitute imported natural gas, reducing reliance on fossil fuels. Initiatives like GOBARDHAN demonstrate the viability of converting organic waste into biomethane for hydrogen production, offering a pathway to diversify feedstock sources, improve energy sovereignty, and integrate waste-to-energy solutions into the fertilizer ecosystem. However, scaling faces aggregation, infrastructure, and cost competitiveness challenges.
forces.source_title: From LNG dependence to domestic resilience: Securing India's fertiliser future

viewpoints.title: India's chemical sector poised for significant growth, boosting industrial gases.
viewpoints.description: The Indian chemical sector, encompassing specialty chemicals and petrochemicals, is projected for substantial expansion, growing from an estimated US$250 billion in 2024 to US$1 trillion by 2040. This robust growth, driven by increasing domestic demand, expanding capacities, and global efforts to de-risk supply chains from China, implies a strong positive outlook for industrial gases. These gases are fundamental raw materials and critical process enablers across various chemical manufacturing segments, ensuring a sustained increase in their consumption.

viewpoints.title: Steel sector's ambitious capacity expansion to significantly drive industrial gas demand.
viewpoints.description: India aims to substantially increase its crude steel capacity from approximately 200 MTPA in FY25 to an ambitious 300-330 MTPA by 2030. This monumental scale-up is expected to involve over INR 10 lakh crore in planned investments by 2030-31. Steelmaking processes, particularly the BF-BOF and EAF/IF routes that constitute the majority of production, are heavily reliant on industrial gases like oxygen and argon. This expansion guarantees a significant and sustained increase in off-take for industrial gas suppliers, offering a very positive growth trajectory.

viewpoints.title: Effective project execution critical for steel capacity, ensuring industrial gas off-take.
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights that successfully achieving India's 300 MTPA steel capacity target by 2030 is highly dependent on institutionalizing execution excellence in capital projects, rather than just capital commitment. Timely commissioning of new steel plants, minimizing delays and cost overruns, directly translates into a predictable and growing demand for industrial gases. If execution falters, project delays could lead to deferred demand for industrial gases, impacting growth forecasts for suppliers.
viewpoints.source_title: Building India’s next 100 MTPA - Embedding execution excellence in steel projects

demand_drivers.description: Increasing focus on sustainable and eco-friendly chemical processes drives demand for green chemicals, many of which involve industrial gases like H2 or CO2.

The strategic shift by global companies away from China-dependent supply chains creates opportunities for India's green chemicals sector, increasing domestic production and industrial gas consumption.

new_opportunities.description: The growth in green chemicals implies a significant demand for industrial hydrogen as a key reagent in various environmentally friendly synthesis processes and for decarbonization initiatives.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Industrial Hydrogen (H2) for green chemical synthesis

new_opportunities.description: Development within the green chemicals market could open new avenues for industrial CO2 utilization in creating sustainable products or for storage as part of broader CCUS efforts.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) applications

market_sizing.methodology: The India green chemicals market is expected to grow at a CAGR of over 10% and exceed US$ 15 billion by 2027. This forecast is driven by rising demand from end-user industries, global de-risking of supply chains from China, and a focus on sustainable production.

demand_drivers.description: Large-scale investments in petrochemical complexes drive significant demand for industrial gases such as oxygen, nitrogen, and hydrogen, which are crucial for processes like oxidation, hydrogenation, and inerting.
The establishment of major petrochemical hubs centralizes demand for bulk industrial gases, fostering long-term take-or-pay contracts and potential for on-site gas production facilities.

market_sizing.methodology: Odisha is targeting investments of Rs 1.2 trillion (US$ 13.6 billion) by 2035 to transform into a leading petrochemical hub. This substantial capital outlay highlights the scale of future petrochemical operations.

demand_drivers.description: Government capital expenditure on major projects (roads, railways, urban infrastructure) creates sustained demand for steel, necessitating increased crude steel production.
Rising demand from vehicle production and broader industrial expansion drives the need for more steel, directly impacting industrial gas consumption in steelmaking.
Growing urban development and housing initiatives contribute significantly to steel demand.

pnl_drivers.driver: Increased demand for Oxygen and Argon
pnl_drivers.description: Both BF-BOF (65% of new capacity) and EAF/IF (35% of new capacity) steelmaking routes heavily rely on oxygen for combustion and refining, and argon for inerting and stirring, directly boosting industrial gas revenues.

market_sizing.methodology: India's crude steel production capacity is projected to increase to 300 MT by FY30, building on 218.29 MT in FY26. This target is part of the National Steel Policy (NSP).

demand_drivers.description: The global push for reducing carbon emissions, particularly in heavy industries, drives the adoption of green steel production methods, which often involve hydrogen as a reducing agent.
Construction, infrastructure, and automotive sectors are expected to increase their procurement of green steel, translating this demand into higher production volumes.

new_opportunities.description: The forecasted massive growth in green steel, especially via hydrogen-based DRI, creates a new and substantial long-term market for industrial hydrogen, fundamental to these cleaner processes.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Industrial Hydrogen (H2) for direct reduced iron (DRI)

market_sizing.methodology: India's green steel demand is forecasted to climb from negligible levels today to 4.49 million tonnes (MT) by FY30, 24 MT by FY35, 73 MT by FY40, and peaking at 179 MT by FY50.
